summary: Burst of 5xx responses from api-gateway during ephemeral proxy CPU-throttle leading to elevated error rate
description:
Issue summary: At ~2026-03-10T15:22:00Z BrightCart began reporting a sharp increase in 5xx responses from our hosted API for dedicated tenants. Impact: Customer saw ~18% of requests return 5xx over a 9-minute window; several streaming sessions dropped mid-response, causing failed checkout recommendations. Environment: Production dedicated pool for BrightCart in us-west-2; traffic mix was embedding + chat streaming during a daytime traffic spike.

Observed behavior: API Gateway returned 502/503/504 intermittently. Upstream serving-runtime logs showed multiple ephemeral-proxy worker threads experiencing CPU throttle spikes followed by short-lived watchdog restarts. Metric correlation shows ephemeral-proxy CPU burn coinciding with accept-queue growth and increased keepalive resets.

Expected behavior: Self-healing proxies should retry without cascading 5xx and should not trigger runtime watchdog restarts for short CPU bursts.

This ticket captures the customer-facing summary, investigative notes, and follow-up actions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route sustained mixed embedding+streaming traffic to a dedicated pool configured with ephemeral proxy enabled (replica set sized to customer commit).
2) Simulate 3x normal request rate for 5 minutes with long-lived streaming sessions (average idle between tokens ~150ms).
3) Observe api-gateway accept-queue growth and ephemeral-proxy thread CPU utilization spike >90% on single cores.
4) Check runtime logs for watchdog restarts, and watch for 502/503/504 responses returned to client.
logs: 2026-03-10T15:22:41Z proxy[ephemeral-7] WARN: thread0 CPU spiked to 94% - queue length 128 - initiating soft-throttle
2026-03-10T15:22:43Z runtime[svc-rt-3] ERROR: upstream response stream aborted: watch_dog_kill(signal=SIGUSR1) pid=4512
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Confirmed elevated 5xx correlated with BrightCart's spike window; not a customer SDK issue.

SRE findings: Ephemeral-proxy threads were single-core bound. A burst of streaming traffic with tight token pacing created CPU hot paths inside the proxy's framing loop leading to missed keepalive heartbeats and accept-queue backlog.

Hypothesis: Combination of long-lived streaming sessions + high per-connection framing CPU created head-of-line blocking on proxy threads; watchdog treats this as unhealthy leading to restarts and upstream 5xx amplification.

Further evidence: No GPU OOMs or serving runtime OOMs observed. Kernel IO and network metrics normal. Replicated locally by replaying production trace with similar token cadence; reproduced accept-queue growth and proxy thread starvation.
mitigations_taken: 1) Temporarily shifted BrightCart traffic to a sibling dedicated pool in us-east-1 to restore service while investigation continued.
2) Increased ephemeral-proxy worker threads for the affected pool to widen concurrency and reduce per-thread CPU load (hotfix deployed to prod at 2026-03-10T15:40Z).
3) Applied a short-term config change to lower streaming token pacing for that customer via rate-limiter rule to avoid immediate re-triggering of watchdog.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: traffic shifted and proxy worker count increased. Error rate dropped to baseline within 6 minutes after mitigations. Root-cause analysis pending to address proxy single-threaded hot-paths and watchdog sensitivity.
resolution_notes: Workaround restored customer traffic to healthy state; BrightCart confirmed recover via CS call at 15:55Z.
SRE to follow up with kernel-level profiling and a runtime patch to make proxy framing loop more yield-friendly and to add soft backpressure before watchdog escalation.
Planned follow-ups: PR with proxy loop yield and thread-affinity fixes, canary in staging, rollout across dedicated pools, update runbook to include automatic traffic re-route thresholds.
next_steps: 1) SRE: produce flame graphs from production trace and submit PR with targeted micro-yields in proxy framing loop (owner: Rafael Ortiz, due 2026-03-15).
2) Runtime team: adjust watchdog threshold for short-term CPU spikes to avoid aggressive restarts (owner: Priya Desai, due 2026-03-18).
3) Support: schedule post-incident call with BrightCart and provide timeline and mitigation summary (owner: Ava Kim, due 2026-03-12).
4) Product: evaluate offering an embedding+streaming admission control guideline for dedicated customers to avoid combined worst-case pacing patterns (owner: Morgan Lee, due 2026-04-01).
